mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an easing monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 delivers negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of months with declining FEDFUNDS, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of months with UNRATE increase > 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate broad demand contraction that triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Negative return signal fails when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, evidenced by positive 20-day returns in >50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals manufacturing sector weakness that reduces corporate profit visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 delivers positive 60-day returns in >60% of periods when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly expansion in real GDP (GDPC1 > 0.5% q/q) signals robust economic growth that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in >50% of quarters with GDPC1 growth >0.5% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflation that triggers Federal Reserve tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in >60% of months with CPIAUCSL YoY >2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate labor market stress that reduces household income and consumption, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Negative return signal fails when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, evidenced by positive 5-day returns in >50% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 2.0% signals active monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 delivers positive 20-day returns in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0%.
